QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_33

question.text: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations 2012 and SEBI circulars, if the Investment Manager fails to achieve First Close within 12 months from the date of SEBI intimation, the AIF must:

answer.text: Automatically convert to a Category I registration.
File for a fresh application for launch.
Halve the committed management fee retrospectively.
Refund double the set-up cost to LPs.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 7.2 'Unsuccessful First Close': 'If the Investment Manager is not able to achieve First Close within 12 months from the date of SEBI intimation, the AIF will have to file for a fresh application for launch. This may delay the deployment of funds, especially during favourable market conditions.' The Trap: Category conversion (A), fee-cut (C) and refund (D) are not SEBI-mandated consequences of a missed First Close. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-A test the same 12-month First Close rule. Memorise: 12 months from SEBI intimation = critical deadline.
